comments.note: Intentional duplication of renderWithAPI (~40 lines × 3 files) is well-reasoned and correctly documented in the Developer and QA pipeline comments. The WP spec explicitly rejected a shared extract to avoid coupling. The duplication is stable and low-maintenance — no action required.

The polling-busy-wait pattern (Date.now() loop + setTimeout 10–15 ms) is consistent across all three files and is the correct approach for jsdom environments. The 200–300 ms timeout windows are generous enough to avoid flakiness without materially slowing CI.

The timer-based busy-wait inside renderWithAPI stops as soon as 'Loading runs' disappears from the #orchestrator-runs-section, which is a precise and reliable signal. The additional `for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) await Promise.resolve()` microtask drain in the queue-aware flush helpers is a good defensive pattern against multi-hop promise chains.

The comment block in project-detail-poll-modes.test.ts (lines 192–208) explaining WHY focus state is tested via element survival rather than document.activeElement is an exemplary test rationale comment — it pre-empts the natural follow-up question from any future contributor.
The `makeQueueEntry` factory in project-detail-runs.test.ts correctly isolates queue-entry construction and makes the AC-1/AC-2 tests easy to read. Good use of the factory pattern in test helpers.

[documentation-forward] The three sibling test files (project-detail-runs.test.ts, project-detail-resume.test.ts, project-detail-poll-modes.test.ts) are not mentioned in any top-level README or TESTING.md document. The project-detail-runs.test.ts header comment cross-references the siblings, but there is no single discovery point for contributors new to the test suite. Consider adding a short entry to the gui test directory README (or creating one) that maps each file to the feature area it covers.

[documentation-forward] The `renderWithAPI` helper signature (apiStubs parameter bag) is duplicated verbatim in all three files. If a new API stub key is added to the production code in future, a contributor must update three files. A short note in each file's JSDoc comment — or in a TESTING.md — listing the stub keys and cross-referencing the other files would reduce the risk of silent omission.
